input.reasoning_summary:
Upon reconsideration, the evidence does support the claim that Bottling Investments is a drag on overall profitability. 

Evidence E2 explicitly states that Bottling Investments consists of finished product operations which "generate higher net operating revenues but lower gross profit margins than concentrate operations." This is a direct statement from the filing about the structural profitability disadvantage of the Bottling Investments segment.

Evidence E4 shows that in 2025, Bottling Investments contributed only 3.1% of total operating income, which is by far the lowest among all operating segments (EMEA 31.2%, Latin America 27.2%, North America 36.8%, Asia Pacific 14.9%). This disproportionately low contribution to operating income, combined with the explicit statement that this segment has lower margins than concentrate operations, supports the characterization that it is a "drag on overall profitability."

The term "drag" in a business context reasonably means a segment that pulls down overall profitability metrics due to lower margins or returns, not necessarily that it loses money. The evidence establishes both that (1) Bottling Investments structurally has lower margins than the concentrate business, and (2) it contributes minimally to operating income relative to other segments. Together, these facts support the claim that the segment is a drag on overall profitability.

The initial verdict was incorrect in requiring evidence of negative profitability or explicit characterization. The combination of the structural margin disadvantage and minimal operating income contribution is sufficient to support this interpretive claim.
